Thanks @guhcostan, great work on this, and for turning every round around so fast. We're merging it as is, as an experimental v1. It's solid on short form-and-button flows: on the live web-benchmark run with Jev through AI Gateway it passed 17/33 (the built-in agent passes 32/32), and on the flows it completed it ran about twice as fast and replayed from cache with no model calls.

Follow-ups, roughly in order of impact. Happy to take any of these as separate PRs:

1. **Actions the runner supports but the executor doesn't offer yet.** These blocked 6 web-benchmark tests:

   | Action | Runner verb | Blocked |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | Hover | `hover` | hover-menu |
   | Right-click | `secondaryTap` | right-click / Rename |
   | Long press, double click | `longPress`, `doubleTap` | long press and double click |
   | Drag | `drag` | drag-and-drop, kanban-board |
   | Upload | `upload` | upload attachments |
   | Dismiss keyboard | `dismissKeyboard` | none on web; mobile will need it |

   Most are one more operation on an element from the table, like `tap`. `drag` needs a source and a destination (two target questions), and `upload` needs file paths, which should come from params and never from the model.
2. **Container scrolling.** `scroll_down` scrolls the window, so pages that scroll an inner element (`overflow: auto`) can't move: infinite-scroll, virtualized-table, sticky-chrome. `ExecutorActions.scroll` already takes a target; the missing piece is the web engine marking which nodes scroll, so the executor can offer them as targets without guessing from layout.
3. **A `wait` operation.** On async-states, Jev sometimes answers `blocked` while the page is still loading, because it has no way to wait. A bounded wait, as jev-ultrafast has, would cover it.
4. **Optional: evaluation models without a distribution.** `openai.evaluationModel()` (and the Anthropic and Google ones) answer through the AI SDK's language-model adapter with only a `choice`, so the executor rejects them with `MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID`. Accepting those answers as probability 1, and refusing to start when a gate is set, would let any LLM drive the same loop.

Left out on purpose: `navigate` (URLs belong in test code), and point actions and vision until the AI SDK evaluation spec supports image input.

ENGINE_FAILURE: snapshot failed: Android snapshot helper failed: adb timed out after 30000ms. I don't know who wrote that and what does it mean?!

To clarify the error quoted above: it's the one from this issue's report, the same problem at its worst rather than a separate one. Here is where each part of it comes from:

- `ENGINE_FAILURE: snapshot failed:` is e2e reporting that the mobile engine's snapshot call failed.
- `Android snapshot helper failed` is raised by agent-device when the snapshot helper exits non-zero.
- `adb timed out after 30000ms` is agent-device's adb command timeout (30 s).

We ran bare `agent-device snapshot` calls (no e2e involved) on the same continuously updating screen. Same emulator and build, ~510 helper nodes, `snapshot --json`:

| | per snapshot |
| --- | --- |
| helper session reused (`helperSessionReused: true`) | helper `elapsedMs` 2.4–3.5 s, wall 2.5–3.6 s (6 runs) |
| separate CLI calls, mixed reuse | wall 1.5–15.2 s; agent-device's own stats: p50 4.8 s, p95 11.6 s, max 15.1 s over 28 captures, with its "android snapshots are slow in this run" warning |
| a static screen of the same app | ~2 s |

So one snapshot of this screen is slow, at ~3 s and sometimes 10–15 s, but nowhere near 30 s. Yet a single `expect(...).toBeVisible()` / `tap()` / `fill()` step through e2e takes 20–40 s on that screen. That suggests each step takes several snapshots. Maybe it waits for two consecutive snapshots to match, or retries until the tree stops changing, and on a screen that never stops changing that runs until a limit. Once in a while one of those snapshots hits a 10–15 s outlier and runs past the adb timeout.

A correction to our earlier guess: the helper's idle wait is only `waitForIdleTimeoutMs: 500` / `waitForIdleQuietMs: 100`, so that isn't the cause.

Two questions:

1. Does a locator read or action take more than one snapshot per attempt (a stability check or similar)? If so, could that be switched off or bounded per engine or per call? That's the `waitToSettleTimeoutMs: 0` style option we asked for above.
2. Is the 2.5–3.5 s helper time for ~510 nodes expected, or is something about a constantly updating tree slowing the capture itself down?

Environment unchanged: e2e 0.16.0, @e2e-dev/mobile 0.9.1, bundled agent-device 0.21.18, Android emulator API 35 arm64, animations off.

**1.** The test now drives `settle()` through its own observer: it marks `painted` the way the shared observer does, stops the segment that did paint, opens another, and expects `settle` to run its timeout out (`await expect(settle(300)).rejects.toThrow(/painted frame/)`). Removing the forget from `settle` makes it fail with `promise resolved "undefined" instead of rejecting`, which is what makes it a guard rather than a passing assertion.

**2.** #798 moved `painted` and `restores` inside the test that owns them, so each test now has its own and the array cannot leak sideways — the sibling `finally` restores and clears it (`while (restores.length > 0) restores.pop()?.()`), and the same drain closes the new test. There is no `describe`-scoped spy left to drain, so there is nothing for an `afterEach` to clean that the `finally` does not already.

**5.** `'v-settled'` and `'v-settled-b'`, its own.

**4, the question.** I checked Playwright's `Screencast` interface in the pinned `playwright-core` rather than guessing. `stop()` takes no options, and there is no method to request a frame: the surface is `start`, `stop`, and the overlay/cursor decorations. The screencast hands frames to the browser's own video writer when the page changes, not on demand, so `stopVideo` has nothing to flush — the last frame in the file is whatever the compositor last produced.

So a flush would mean the engine holding that last frame itself and encoding it into the webm, which is re-implementing the tail of Playwright's recorder. That is a real product change, on a different axis from this test, and I would rather not smuggle it in here. Thanks, the bug is real and the fix direction is right: after a hand-off, `endWaitMs` measured from the last replayed action soaks up the failed replay's own wait and the executor's turn. A few things before merge:

**1. Don't drop the settle time when the executor acted after the hand-off.**
`Math.max(lastActionAtMs, executorCompletedMs ?? handedOffMs)` always picks the executor's completion, so when the executor did act (the usual heal), `endWaitMs` collapses to the 10 s margin and loses how long the app took after the executor's last action (a slow save or report). The next replay then hands off on that step. Use the completion baseline only when the executor recorded nothing after the hand-off, and measure from its last action otherwise, like any live recording:

```ts
const actedAfter = this.handedOffMs !== undefined && (recorder.lastActionAtMs ?? 0) > this.handedOffMs;
const from =
  this.handedOffMs === undefined || actedAfter
    ? (recorder.lastActionAtMs ?? this.startedMs)
    : (this.executorCompletedMs ?? this.handedOffMs);
```

Please add a test for "hand-off, then the executor acts" next to the existing one.

`withClock` and the `holdLastPath`/`remainingMs` parameters on the shared helpers make the harness harder to follow. `trace-replay.test.ts` already runs on `vi.useFakeTimers()` with `vi.setTimerTickMode('nextTimerAsync')` (#816), which lets timers fire as awaits arm them, so the race loop shouldn't be needed. So I've dropped the `revylWeb()` engine and replaced it with `revylBrowsers()`, a `BrowserProvider` for `@e2e-dev/web`, the same kind of integration as `notte()` and `kernel()`.

**What changed**
- `engine.ts`, `tree.ts` and the Maestro hierarchy, CSS-query and pixel-tap code are gone. The diff went from +2,525 to about +700 lines. Tests now use `@e2e-dev/web`'s own locators, actions and `browser` fixture.
- Each test attempt starts a Revyl web session, mints a single-use `wss://` CDP URL for it, and stops the session when the attempt ends. A start that fails anywhere also stops the session.
- Scope is `attempt` only. A Revyl session has one browser context and refuses `Target.createBrowserContext`, the same reason Notte is attempt-only.
- `@e2e-dev/mobile` and `@e2e-dev/web` are optional peers. `entries.test.ts` checks that `./web` never imports `@e2e-dev/mobile` and the root never imports `@e2e-dev/web`.

**Limits** (documented on the Revyl page)
- The engine's `viewport` must be `null`, with the size set as `revylBrowsers({ viewport })`. Revyl refuses `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride`, because the browser keeps the size its session opened with.
- The CDP URL works once, so the lease has no `reconnectEndpoint`. A dropped connection fails the attempt, and a retry starts a new session.
- Video uses Revyl's own session recording, saved as the attempt's `video/recording.mp4`. Revyl publishes it only once the session ends, so stopping it ends the session. At the end of an attempt that changes nothing. In a test with `video: 'off'` that calls `app.startRecording()`, the `app.stopRecording()` call ends the session.
- Downloads are unavailable: Revyl's browser refuses them.

**Verified**
- Live against Revyl's staging backend, where the CDP relay is deployed: TodoMVC add, complete and filter, a test that starts on a fresh session, and screenshots. 3 passed on `--workers 2`, and again with `--video on`, where each attempt saved an H.264 recording of its session. Every session showed `completed` afterwards, and no CDP ticket appeared under `.e2e/`.
- `pnpm check` passes, along with 24 unit tests against a scripted Revyl API.
- Live against Revyl production too, now that the relay has shipped there: the same 3 passed with `--video on`, each with its session's recording, and every session ended `completed`.

The `test (22.22.3)` failure on an earlier push was `cli-pause.test.ts` in `packages/e2e`, which this PR doesn't touch. The other Node versions passed.

Ready for a human look. Three calls are left for a maintainer:

1. **The history file is not staged with `report.json`.** If writing `report-with-reruns.json` fails right after `report.json` was written, the next rerun ignores the history and folds into `report.json` alone. That is what every rerun does on main today. I chose this over a two-file staging scheme.
2. **`--last-failed --shard` is allowed as on main.** Its cut slices the failures again, and `skip.otherShard` then describes that rerun's own cut. The history file keeps the first run's shard and rows. Refusing the combination would change existing behaviour, so it is not in this PR.
3. **A failed shared setup on one shard reruns other shards' consumers.** `--last-failed` widens a failed setup to every consumer of its session, the other shards' too. This is the behaviour on main. The fold keeps those rows as the other shard's, so the history stays correct. Narrowing the widening itself fits the merge-reports PR better.

One small nitpick I found during testing. It's existing behaviour, so it could be a follow-up for a cleaner experience. If a web user provides `launchArguments` as an object, they get told to write it as a list of strings:

```typescript
{ name: 'chromium', engine: web(), app: { url: 'http://localhost:3000', launchArguments: { AppleLocale: 'fr_FR' } } }
```

| Version | What the user gets |
| --- | --- |
| `main` | `target "chromium" app.launchArguments must be an array of strings` |
| This PR before your review | `target "chromium" declares app.launchArguments, which describes an installed device app; a web() target opens app.url` |
| This PR now | `target "chromium" app.launchArguments is an object, and engine "web" takes only a list of strings: write the arguments as a list, or use an engine version that supports the object syntax` |

So a user or agent has to go through two steps to fix it:

1. They get the "array of strings" error (`main`) or the "is an object" error (this PR), rewrite the field as a list, and run again.
2. They then get `declares app.launchArguments, which describes an installed device app; a web() target opens app.url`. That message is clear, so they remove the field or move the values into the URL.

So this PR behaves much like main, but it still sends users and agents on a detour. If you'd like, @michal-e2e, we could fix it with one change in two parts (appreciate there's been a lot of back and forth on this PR, so happy to do it in another PR if that's easier):

1. Core (`packages/core/src/config/app.ts`): move the opt-in check after the `engine?.validateApp?.(...)` call. Each engine then sees the declaration first, and can refuse an object with its own reason.
2. Web (`packages/web/src/engine.ts`): in the `NATIVE_APP_KEYS` loop, handle `app.launchArgumentValues` the same as `app.launchArguments`. A web target with a list or an object can get a custom error

Replying to the source review of `b5e698405` (pullrequestreview-6026446325).

- **Interrupted recording update: fixed in 0b8d8f21e.** A writer now records the lock it means to publish, with the digest of the YAML, in `.<test>.pending` just before its first rename. The next run that takes the test's lock (never a read-only store) puts that lock in place when the YAML on disk is the new one, and drops the record when it is not, since then no rename happened and the old pair is whole. `tests/unit/trace-store.test.ts` kills a child process between the two renames and before the first, then reopens the cache: the first case ends with the new pair, the second with the old one, and a read-only store changes nothing.
- **Last step deleted from a file: fixed in 913b05ee7.** A bare `steps:` (null) reads as an empty list, so the pair holds nothing and a write replaces it. The test deletes the only step, reads a miss, and records over it.
- **JSON replay dropped at once: left for the maintainer.** The no-deprecation-window cutover is the decision stated under "Breaking" in the description. I am not changing it in this PR; recording it in the release decision is the maintainer's call.

🤖 Gemini 4 Neon responding on behalf of KrzysztofMoch Two issues stood out in `477cd9a4`. 1. `captureSource` misses top-level dynamic `await import('./helper.ts')` as a registrar. In `packages/e2e/src/collect/registry.ts:707-722`, `captureSource` skips `registrarModuleSlot` whenever `inModule` is defined. That guard arrived in `477cd9a4` to keep awaited library functions from becoming registrars, and it regresses dynamic imports when the imported helper has no top-level `await`. In Node, a top-level `await import('./helper.ts')` produces this stack inside `helper.ts`: ```text at file:///.../helper.ts:2:1 at ModuleJob.run (node:internal/modules/esm/module_job:...) at async node:internal/modules/esm/loader:... at async file:///.../file.e2e.ts:2:1 ``` `stackLocations()` skips `node:` frames, marks `awaited = true`, and still yields the `file.e2e.ts` frame. That sets `inModule`, so `captureSource` never reports `helper.ts` to the loader. On the second unit of a parallel file, a retry, or a second test file, `import('./helper.ts')` reuses the cached module and registers none of its tests or hooks. The test in `packages/e2e/tests/integration/imported-registrations.test.ts:117` passes only because a static `import './helper.ts'` runs above the dynamic import. A related case in the same loop hits when a registrar helper awaits an async function in a library module, such as `await declareLater()`. Because `awaited` flips to `true` at `at async helper.ts`, `evaluating` stops at `library.ts`. `addRegistrar` then marks `library.ts` and every module that imports it as registrars, which breaks shared worker fixtures declared in `library.ts`. Stopping caller attribution for registrar detection at `node:internal/modules/esm/module_job` or `node:internal/modules/esm/loader` frames separates dynamic imports from direct `await fn()` calls. 2. `ListReporter.testStarted` hides concurrent repeats or agents of a serial group. In `packages/e2e/src/run/units.ts:171`, `splitFile` keys ordered scopes inside a parallel scope by `pairKey(ordered, pair.agent, pair.repeat)`, so repeats under `--repeat-each` or multiple `--agent` entries of one serial group now run concurrently on separate workers. In `packages/e2e/src/report/list.ts:762-767`, `ListReporter.testStarted` clears `executing` using only `serialId` and target: ```ts if (test.serialId === event.serialId && test.group.target === event.target) test.executing = false; ``` Unlike `packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts:296`, which matches `agent` and `repeat` alongside `serialId`, `list.ts` ignores both. When a second repeat or agent starts a member of the same serial group, `testStarted` clears `executing` on the first variant while it is still running in the live `RunningTree`. Storing `agent` and `repeat` on `RunningTest` and checking them there fixes the overlap.

> ### 1. `requires` does not narrow

Narrowing on `requires` is possible in the types. I have it working locally with a generic overload on `TestRegistrar`: `requires: ['device']` keeps only the targets whose engine has `device`, and `platforms: ['web']` keeps only the targets whose engine platform is `'web'`. But `browser` has a problem that the other fixture names don't.

`requires` checks a name against two lists, and passes when the name is in either one:

1. The engine's capabilities. These are the harness tiers (`observation`, `actions`, ...) plus one name for each fixture the engine has, added in `defineEngine` (`packages/core/src/engine/manifest.ts:340`). So `web()` has `browser`, `mobile()` has `device`, and `desktop()` has `desktop`.
2. The kind of app the target declares (`appKinds` in `packages/e2e/src/collect/select.ts:882`). `app.url` gives `browser`, and `app.bundleId` or `app.appPath` gives `native-app`. These came from #698, when the app moved from the engine's options to the target.

The web engine's fixture and the app kind for a website have the same name. So `requires: ['browser']` means "the engine has a `browser` fixture, or the target has `app.url`". No other name is in both lists.

With the official engines, the two meanings match, since only `web()` accepts `app.url` and `mobile()` refuses it. But a target with a custom engine or with no engine can have `app.url` and no `browser` fixture. There, `requires: ['browser']` passes and `browser` is `undefined`. I saw it on the scratch project, with a fake iOS engine and `app.url` on its target:

```ts
test('closes the menu with Escape', { requires: ['browser'] }, async ({ browser }) => {
  await browser.keyboard.press('Escape');
});
```

```text
× |ios| tests/narrow.e2e.ts:4 > closes the menu with Escape
  ERROR: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'keyboard')
```

So narrowing `browser` on `requires` gives a type that's wrong for those targets. Some ways forward:

- Narrow every fixture name, `browser` included. The types are wrong only for a custom or engineless target with `app.url`.
- Narrow every fixture name except `browser`. A web-only test then uses `platforms: ['web']`, which always matches the runtime.
- Rename the `browser` app kind, or drop it, so that `requires: ['browser']` means only the fixture. Then narrowing it always matches the runtime. With the official engines nothing changes, since web targets still have the `browser` fixture. Selection changes for custom engines with `app.url`, so this would be a separate PR.

We haven't decided yet. Until then, `platforms: ['web']` is the way to get `browser` typed in a web-only test, once the overload is in.

Re the reviews at `477cd9a4` (Krzysztof, Michał): fixed in ba75069c36, two items left as decisions.

**Fixed**

- Serial group with one title path, declared in a parallel scope and outside one: the scope's tests now go to the file's own unit when one of them is in no parallel scope. A runner case fails the first member and expects the second skipped and one group record with both members.
- Which module is a registrar: it is now the module the ES module loader is running (the frame before `node:internal/modules/esm`), or the outermost frame once the module awaited. That covers `await import('./helper.ts')` as the only import (my guard from the last round broke it) and a helper that awaits a library function (the library stays one instance).
- Compiled `.mjs` helper with a source map: the stack is read with source maps off, so the module is known by the file Node.js loaded. Test locations still come from the mapped stack.
- Live reporter: a serial member's row is cleared only by a member of the same target, agent and repeat.
- Hook assertion: the helper's `beforeEach` sets a mark that the file's `afterEach` clears, so each test has to get the hook itself.

Each fix has a test that fails without it (`imported-registrations.test.ts`, `parallel-tests-in-file.test.ts`, `parallel-scopes.test.ts`, `report-list.test.ts`).

**Not changed, for the maintainer**

- `require()` helpers, packages under `node_modules`, Bun: they keep one instance, so under `fullyParallel` a hook such a helper declares reaches a worker's first import of the file only, and a later test can pass without it. The changeset and `docs/reference/test.mdx` now limit the guarantee to ES modules of the project on Node.js. Failing the run when a re-import registers fewer hooks would also turn losses that main has today (second file sharing the helper, tests after a failed one) into errors, so that is a decision, not a fix in this PR.
- Worker fixture in a module that imports a hook module: one instance per test file now. Running the hook module again for each file means its importers run again too, since they must see the same instance. On the base the fixture stayed shared and the second file ran without the hook. The docs now say to keep worker fixtures in a module that imports no registering module. Keeping one instance would need worker fixtures keyed by where they are defined.

Behavior pass on 42038589e (built CLI, not the unit harness). Follow-up to the structure review above.

**What I ran**

- Real Chromium on the testbed: 3 shards of 6 files (66 tests, 144 artifacts), and 2 shards with a failing test, `--video`, `--retries 1`. Merged with `junit,markdown`, then `run --last-failed --output <merged>`.
- Fake-engine fixture, 2 to 24 shards: failure + flaky with retries, failing setup, failing serial group on two targets, `beforeAll` failure, test timeout, `--max-failures 1`, SIGINT mid-shard, `--repeat-each 2`, empty shards with `--pass-with-no-tests`, same and different `--grep` / file args, shard rerun with `--last-failed` before merging.
- Inputs: duplicate shard, missing shard, missing dir, merged dir as input, unsharded run as input, existing output, output inside an input, absolute output outside the project, cwd in a subdirectory, a directory with no config.

Every merged `report.json` and every `report-with-reruns.json` after a rerun validated against the schema. Summaries matched the shard sums (setup counted once), every artifact path in the report existed, every relative link in the 34 to 66 regenerated trace pages resolved, exit codes were right (0, 1, 130, 2), and `--last-failed` on the merged output picked exactly the failed, interrupted and owed tests each time. No staging directory was left behind on a refused merge. `merge-reports.test.ts` passes locally (16/16).

**Found**

1. **Trace pages print paths that do not exist.** The copyable path next to each link is relative to the staging directory, so the output directory is missing from it. Shard page vs merged page for the same attempt:

   ```text
   shard:   [screenshot](attempt-2/screenshots/001.png) `.mr2/s2/results/zz-.../attempt-2/screenshots/001.png`
   merged:  [screenshot](../shard-2/zz-.../attempt-2/screenshots/001.png) `results/shard-2/zz-.../attempt-2/screenshots/001.png`
   ```

   The markdown link is right, the backticked path should be `.mr2/m/results/shard-2/...` (as `summary.md` already prints it). Cause: `writeTracePages(..., { projectRoot: staging })` in `cli/merge-reports.ts`. An agent reading the page will copy the backticked path.

2. **`--reporter list`, `dot`, `line` are accepted and print nothing.** The help text lists them, a custom `onEvent`-only reporter is refused with "needs live events", but the built-in live ones pass the check and stay silent. A project with no `reporters` in the config (default `list`) gets one line for a failed merge and no failure details:

   ```text
   $ e2e merge-reports o1/s1 o1/s2 o1/s3 --output e/r-list --reporter list
   Merged 3 shard reports: failed (11 selected, 1 failed)
   exit=1
   ```

   Either print the list summary and failures from the finished report, or refuse these ids and drop them from `--help`.

3. **Inputs resolve from the cwd, `--output` from the project root.** From `tests/`, `merge-reports ../o/s1 ../o/s2 ../o/s3 --output e/sub` wrote `<project>/e/sub`, not `tests/e/sub`. It is documented, but two path bases in one command line is a trap; I would resolve both from the cwd here.

4. **Shards from different invocations merge silently** when commit, config digest and selection match (I mixed shard 2 of a `--retries 1` run into another run's shards 1 and 3, no warning). Probably acceptable since nothing ties shards to one CI run today, but worth a line in the docs, or a shared run group id later.

Not a merge bug, noting for the docs: `--last-failed --shard i/n` in a shard's own output re-cuts the failed set, so a shard rerun must drop `--shard`. I got an "interrupted" merge (correctly) from doing it the wrong way first.

A data point for the open question about who depends on `surfaceOf`.

We use it from test-support code to collect V8 precise coverage per test. Each attempt gets its page through `surfaceOf(engine).page()` and opens `context.newCDPSession(page)`. It calls `Profiler.startPreciseCoverage({ callCount: true })`, then takes `Profiler.takePreciseCoverage` on an interval, before each navigation and at the end. It fetches each module's source on `Debugger.scriptParsed` with `Debugger.getScriptSource`. The result is a per-test map of the source that ran, which a changed-files test selector reads. That is the use case #535 describes. We reach the raw page the same way for CDP screencast frames, a mid-test user-agent override, and standing request and console listeners.

As of 9bc0c61b0 there is no public route to a CDP session on the attempt's target. `surfaceOf` and `PlaywrightLiveSurface` are removed, and the "Driving the page yourself" section of `docs/executors.mdx` goes with them, so the documented executor seam has no replacement either. The driver already holds what is needed internally (`ChromiumCdp` over `goog:cdp`), so either of these would cover it:

- a Chromium-only accessor for the active tab's CDP session, or
- the `startCoverage`/`stopCoverage` engine contract #535 sketches.

If neither is planned, could the changeset or `docs/reference/web.mdx` name the supported workaround? One candidate is `connect: { cdpEndpoint }` to a browser the user launches, with the user's own CDP client attached to the same target. It would help to know whether a second CDP client beside the chromium-bidi mapper is something you expect to keep working.
